walkthroughs.body_html:
Biochemistry, Genetics & Evolution — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Biochemistry, Genetics & Evolution brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Biochemistry, Genetics & Evolution.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: An organism with two different alleles at a locus is:
options: Homozygous
Heterozygous
Hemizygous
Polyploid

mcqs.q: A monohybrid cross of two heterozygotes Aa × Aa gives a phenotypic ratio (dominance) of:

options: Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.
Mutations occur because organisms need to adapt to their environment.
Mutations only happen in organisms that have been damaged by external chemicals.
They are random changes in DNA — caused by errors in replication or by mutagens — not directed by need.

mcqs.q: How does a population of organisms become better adapted to its environment over time?
options: Mutations only happen in organisms that have been damaged by external chemicals.
Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.
Individual organisms change during their lifetime in response to their environment and pass the changes on to offspring.
Individuals with advantageous heritable variations survive and reproduce more; their alleles increase in frequency over generations.
No — humans and chimpanzees share a common ancestor; both have evolved from it.
Mutations only happen in organisms that have been damaged by external chemicals.
Humans evolved directly from chimpanzees, which is why chimps still exist as a less-evolved version.
Humans evolved from monkeys but chimps evolved from gorillas.
